Display names were read back from the platform: 240 properties and 73 relations named in the sample's language, the rules and adjustments toolboxes with their functions, no ID-style toolbox left.

The sample's Workshop app was created and published by the installation, its rule functions resolved to this installation's rules toolbox; it was opened in Workshop with its rule results, and created again after reinstallation. In the browser a scenario was saved and checked for applying but not applied; the adjust actions it runs were executed through Context Loader.

The four rule functions are mounted on the network and were called through Context Loader execute_tool and through the toolbox proxy the Workshop schedule Gantt uses; every check result matched the same code run locally on the package fixtures.

The two adjust actions were executed through Context Loader (get_action_info, execute_action, get_action_execution); their writes were read back with Cypher and then restored. Installing again restores the package schedule.
Reference queries, graph patterns, functions and actions were checked through APIs, and the Workshop app was opened and checked in Workshop; no model answered the questions.

Opening the app in the browser on this 0.1.11 package, its four rule functions completed their checks in about 12 s (29 tasks in the window, hard 11, late 8, kit 5, capability 1, operator 8, changeover 8, not checked 0); dates showed as dates, the check detail opened on the failing rule, and a test scenario (a maintenance work order moved one day) was saved and its apply dialog named the conflict by work order, operation and machine and blocked applying; nothing was applied and the scenario was deleted.

The app file is unchanged from 0.1.10, where the app was exported, imported as a new app with made-up toolbox and function IDs, and its four rule functions were found by toolbox and function name and completed their checks; the copies were deleted.
